title: Better together: Cut your GitHub Actions build times by up to 90% with Bitrise Build Hub and Build Cache
summary: Build Hub and Build Cache sit in the same data centers, so GitHub Actions jobs run on faster machines that only compile what's changed: up to 90% faster builds.
body_markdown:
## Mobile builds on GitHub Actions are slow for two reasons


Your mobile CI can be slow for several reasons, but the two biggest issues we see affecting build times on GitHub Actions across thousands of mobile projects are a lack of raw compute and cold builds. And fixing one in isolation won't deliver the performance improvements needed in today's climate, as AI agents push more code through your pipeline than ever before.


Let's break it down:


### 1) The machines


GitHub's hosted Mac runners top out at M2 Pro, with 5 vCPUs and 14 GB of RAM, and jobs can sit in a queue at peak times.


On a weak machine, every stage of the pipeline stretches: compiling, testing and archiving all take longer, and tight memory can slow large builds further or make them fail.


Longer jobs hold runners for longer, so queues build up behind them. PR checks come back late, so developers wait, switch context, or merge with less confidence.


Over a day, that adds up to fewer builds, slower feedback and later releases. Over a week or a month it has a detrimental impact on your release schedule affecting your go-to-market, customer experience and competitive position.


### 2) Cache that always starts cold


GitHub gives each repo 10 GB of cache, but for many engineering teams this is nowhere near enough capacity to be effective. DerivedData from Xcode alone can eat up to 20 GB or more, so even your prized 'cached' builds may often start cold, compiling every artifact for every build.


And GitHub Actions' default dependency cache stores DerivedData/compilation cache as one big archive, so if anything in it changes, **the whole archive has to be uploaded again.** With Bitrise Build Cache, only the objects that changed are uploaded, and only the ones needed for the build are downloaded.


With AI coding agents, both issues are compounded at an alarming rate. Our[State of Mobile Development 2026](https://bitrise.io/reports/state-of-mobile-development-2026) report shows that AI-authored builds have grown **161x in just 12 months** with agents pushing more commits and CI runs.


## Our mobile expertise


We've spent over a decade building CI infrastructure purpose-built for mobile: powerful Apple silicon and Linux machines with the latest Xcode versions (available within 24 hours), plus preinstalled Android SDKs and tooling that compute-heavy mobile builds depend on.


That experience led to the development of[Bitrise Build Hub](https://bitrise.io/platform/build-hub) (runners) and[Bitrise Build Cache](https://bitrise.io/platform/build-cache) (remote caching) which solve and eliminate these problems head-on, **resulting in up to 90% faster builds** for everyone on your team.

## Why Build Hub and Build Cache are better together


### Faster machines doing less work


Bitrise Build Hub runs your CI jobs on the fastest, mobile-optimized Mac ([M5 Pro and M6](https://bitrise.io/blog/post/m5-pro-runners-live-github-actions) ) and Linux machines. An M5 Pro X-Large job gets 18 vCPU and 54 GB of RAM, compared with 5 vCPU and 14 GB on GitHub's largest macOS runner. On the open-source DuckDuckGo iOS project, that resulted in 72% faster builds: 2m 27s instead of 8m 43s.


[Bitrise Build Cache](https://bitrise.io/platform/build-cache) then makes sure those machines only compile new work by storing previous build outputs instead of starting from scratch. In benchmarks on open-source Android and iOS projects, Build Cache cut build times by up to 83% for Bazel, 72% for Gradle and 55% for Xcode.


**Together, they speed up your builds significantly.**


Our runners and build cache sit in the same Bitrise data centers, in the US or EU. Cache hits travel a shorter distance, so they come back faster and cost $0 in egress. Even better, there's no token to manage either: Build Hub runners authenticate to Build Cache automatically via our CLI using your Bitrise account.


The result is **builds up to 90% faster,** with every build using fewer minutes allowing your monthly budget to go further.

## How to get started


Getting started takes a free trial, a machine pool and two small changes to a workflow you already have.


1. [Sign up for a free trial](https://app.bitrise.io/users/sign_up?product=build-hub) , and start Build Hub and Build Cache on the same day, so one evaluation covers both.
2. In Bitrise, open Build Hub and[create a machine pool](https://docs.bitrise.io/en/bitrise-build-hub/build-hub-for-github-actions/creating-machine-pools-for-github-actions) : install the Bitrise - Build Hub GitHub app on your organization, then pick a machine type and image. Bitrise labels the pool` bitrise-runner-<pool-name>` .
3. Point the job at Build Hub by setting its` runs-on` label to that pool.
4. Add two steps that install the Bitrise Build Cache CLI and activate the cache for your build tool.


**There's no token to add: the runner is already connected to your Bitrise workspace.**


Rather hand it to an AI coding agent? Our[setup prompt](https://docs.bitrise.io/en/bitrise-build-cache/getting-started-with-the-build-cache/getting-started-with-ai) does the install for you.


```text
jobs:
build:
runs-on:     bitrise-runner-ios
steps:
-     uses:     actions/checkout@v4
-     name:     Install     the     Bitrise     Build     Cache     CLI
run:     curl     --retry     5     -sSfL     'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitrise-io/bitrise-build-cache-cli/main/install/installer.sh'     |     sh     -s     --     -b     /tmp/bin     -d
-     name:     Activate     Bitrise     Build     Cache     for     Xcode
run:     /tmp/bin/bitrise-build-cache     activate     xcode     --cache     --cache-push
-     name:     Build
run:     xcodebuild     build     -workspace     MyApp.xcworkspace     -scheme     MyApp
```
